items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5

clusters.headline: Deno is joining Cloudflare

items.title: Deno is joining Cloudflare
items.extract: Deno is joining Cloudflare The Deno team released the first version of celld back in August - their open source implementation of the Durable Objects pattern from Cloudflare Workers. Today, Cloudflare are acquiring Deno outright, with the goal of building on celld to "make workerd self-hosting a first-class supported way to build and run apps using the Workers programming model" (see the Cloudflare blog .) The bad news is that Deno itself will not be maintained by Cloudflare beyond the next year: We will support the Deno runtime for another year with monthly releases containing bug fixes and security updates. After that year we will end our development of the Deno runtime.

clusters.summary: Cloudflare is acquiring Deno outright. As part of this deal, the Deno team will build on their open-source celld implementation—released in August as their version of the Durable Objects pattern from Cloudflare Workers—to make workerd self-hosting a first-class supported way to build and run apps using the Workers programming model. Cloudflare will support the Deno runtime for another year through monthly releases that include bug fixes and security updates. Following this one-year period, Cloudflare will discontinue development of the Deno runtime.

clusters.headline: ttok 1.0

items.title: ttok 1.0
items.extract: Release: ttok 1.0 I released ttok 0.4 , ran uv tool upgrade ttok , piped a file into the new version... and realized that it was defaulting to the GPT-4 tokenizer when it should very clearly default to GPT-5/GPT-6 instead! I figured switching the default was a reasonable excuse to finally ship a 1.0. OpenAI haven't actually confirmed that GPT-6 uses the same tokenizer as the GPT-5 family yet - there's an angry issue about it - but I found this commit by William Liu which reports on an experiment he ran confirming that the tokenizers are likely the same: All seven GPT models (5.5, 5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, 6 Astra/Sol/Luna) report 44,794 tokens and match each other on every one of the 31 fixtures.

clusters.summary: The software tool ttok 1.0 has been released. The creator upgraded to version 1.0 after realizing the previous version defaulted to the GPT-4 tokenizer instead of GPT-5 or GPT-6. While OpenAI has not confirmed that GPT-6 shares a tokenizer with the GPT-5 family, a commit by William Liu reports an experiment confirming the tokenizers are likely identical. Specifically, all seven GPT models—versions 5.5, 5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna, as well as version 6 Astra, Sol, and Luna—report 44,794 tokens and match each other across all 31 fixtures.

clusters.headline: 6 Guidelines for Governing AI

items.title: 6 Guidelines for Governing AI
items.extract: For the first 10 years of my career, I worked in product management and data analytics by myself. I wrote database queries that pulled numbers out of corporate systems, built statistical models to predict what customers would buy, and shipped data pipelines that moved information between business systems. I built and scaled analytics teams at Best Buy and Target , studying how customers shop and what stores should stock. Today I lead enterprise AI transformation at Lowe’s , the Fortune 100 home improvement retailer. The goal is not to sell artificial intelligence ; it is to use it to deliver useful expertise at the moment a customer needs it.

clusters.summary: Lowe's enterprise AI transformation leader published six guidelines for governing artificial intelligence, according to the headline. The author spent the first 10 years of their career working independently in product management and data analytics, writing database queries, building statistical models for customer purchasing predictions, and shipping data pipelines. They also built and scaled analytics teams at Best Buy and Target, where they studied customer shopping habits and store inventory needs. Today, they lead enterprise AI transformation at the Fortune 100 home improvement retailer Lowe's. The stated goal at Lowe's is to use artificial intelligence to provide useful expertise when customers need it, rather than selling the technology itself.

clusters.headline: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception

items.title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
items.extract: Recent incidents have highlighted the challenge of monitoring LLM agents and the danger of models deceiving people. We show that white-box deception detection via probes can be scaled up to frontier monitoring settings by collecting the largest deception dataset to date for training probes and introducing a novel probe architecture which can aggregate information across many layers and tokens. Our probes achieve 98.8% AUC in SHADE-Arena, surpassing an Opus 5.5 text-monitoring baseline, and show improved efficacy as the underlying model is scaled up. To push our probes to their limit, we test them on several cases where deception cannot be determined from the context alone.

clusters.summary: Probes have been successfully demonstrated to detect sabotage and unverbalized deception in large language models. This white-box detection method was scaled up by gathering the largest deception dataset to date to train probes and by introducing a new probe architecture capable of aggregating information across multiple layers and tokens. The resulting probes achieved an AUC of 98.8% in SHADE-Arena, outperforming an Opus 5.5 text-monitoring baseline, and demonstrated enhanced effectiveness as the underlying model scale increased. Furthermore, these probes were tested on multiple scenarios where context alone could not determine deception.

clusters.summary: Astrophysicist Brice Ménard of Johns Hopkins University utilized Anthropic's Claude Science to generate the first complete ultraviolet map of the entire sky. Autonomous AI agents retrieved data across various space missions, performed calibration, and applied inpainting to complete missing regions. The resulting predictions demonstrated an average deviation of approximately ten percent when compared against actual measurements. Ménard noted that this specific research initiative would not have been accomplished without the assistance of artificial intelligence.

Meanwhile, the Iranian "Bogus Bylines" effort employed seven fictitious reporters to publish nearly 100 articles across online media platforms globally.
